title: The habit architecture that survives month 3
caption: Motivation gets you to week 3. Architecture gets you to year 1. The 5-part system that actually holds. Save this.

slides.headline: The habit architecture that survives
slides.sub: Where every streak app fails — and why.

slides.title: Decide in calm, not in the moment
slides.body: The brain at 6am is not the brain that committed at 9pm. Make the decision once, in advance, specific enough that the 6am brain has nothing to negotiate.

slides.title: Mechanism, not memory
slides.body: A habit you only 'remember' fails under stress. Bind it to a mechanism you can't quietly skip — laid-out gear, a booked slot, a person expecting you.

slides.title: Track compliance, not streaks
slides.body: Aim for 28-of-30, not a perfect chain. Streak psychology means one miss feels like total failure → you quit. Compliance windows survive the miss.

slides.title: Asymmetric modes
slides.body: A slip drops you to half-intensity for a week. You only return to full after stable compliance — not one good day. Defense easy, aggression earned.

slides.title: The post-slip protocol
slides.body: What you do AFTER a miss matters more than the miss. Not 'restart the streak' — a 4-minute trigger-mapping: what happened, what preceded it, what changes.

slides.quote: Discipline isn't a personality trait. It's an architecture choice.
